edits.event: Federal THC limits for hemp-derived products
edits.dependency: RYTHM bought the brands from Green Thumb in 2025 and licensed them back for fixed fees through August 2030. A repurchase ends the fees on the rights Green Thumb’s affiliate buys back.
edits.why_now: A Green Thumb subsidiary holds a RYTHM note due February 25, 2027. A repurchase following the December hemp deadline could reduce RYTHM’s licensing income as the note comes due.
edits.of: RYTHM’s total 2027 revenue at its Q3 2026 run rate
edits.who: Sanjay Tolia, Independent Director and Audit Committee Chair
edits.opening: Mr. Tolia, RYTHM’s Q3 filing says the December hemp restrictions would satisfy one condition for Green Thumb’s affiliate to repurchase the licensed brands. How is the audit committee assessing a potential repurchase alongside the February note maturity?
edits.why_matters: Green Thumb pays RYTHM $64 million a year for its consumer packaged goods brands and $6 million for the incredibles brand. Together the fees equal about 73% of RYTHM’s Q3 2026 revenue on an annualized basis.
edits.condition: RYTHM says the federal hemp limits would satisfy one eligibility condition for repurchase. Fee revenue would fall only if the applicable conditions were met and Green Thumb’s affiliate chose to exercise its option.
edits.timing: The two five-year option windows end in May and August 2030. The April and July repurchase dates are scenario assumptions.
edits.event_description: Section 781 of Public Law 119-37 counts THCA toward the 0.3% total-THC limit for hemp and caps total THC in finished cannabinoid products at 0.4 mg per container. Products above the applicable limit lose federal hemp status.
edits.event_timing: The limits affecting RYTHM’s products were scheduled for December 11, 2026, the same day federal funding was due to expire. Congress could change that date or amend the limits in the funding bill or separate legislation.

baseline.description: Both agreements continue throughout 2027 at their fixed annual fees. The $70 million baseline excludes inflation adjustments.

scenarios.label: Both licenses end April 1
scenarios.description: After the federal hemp limits take effect, Green Thumb’s affiliate repurchases both sets of brand rights on April 1, 2027. RYTHM earns only the first quarter’s fees.

scenarios.description: Green Thumb’s affiliate repurchases only the consumer packaged goods brands on July 1, 2027. RYTHM earns six months of the $64 million fee and all of the $6 million incredibles fee.

edits.event: WAKIX patent litigation and potential generic entry
edits.dependency: Generic pitolisant would compete with WAKIX. Harmony had settled with six of seven generic applicants. At least one settlement permits early entry under conditions the public excerpt does not specify. Competition from other applicants depends on those terms.
edits.why_now: Peter Anastasiou was due to become CEO on January 1, less than four weeks before the injunction hearing and ahead of Harmony’s 2027 guidance.
edits.of: Harmony’s total 2027 revenue at its Q3 2026 run rate
edits.who: Peter Anastasiou, Senior Executive Vice President and COO, appointed CEO effective January 1, 2027
edits.opening: Peter, congratulations on your appointment. With the AET injunction hearing in January and the 30-month stay expiring in February, how are you accounting for the timing of a possible generic WAKIX launch in the 2027 plan?
edits.why_matters: Harmony earned its entire $268.9 million of Q3 2026 revenue from WAKIX. A March 2027 generic launch would cut modeled annual revenue by $582.6 million. An October launch would cut it by $174.8 million. Both estimates assume WAKIX retains 35% of its prior sales rate after entry.
edits.condition: Generic entry requires FDA approval and a decision by AET and Sandoz to launch. The larger shortfall assumes the court rules for AET on the ’197 and ’947 patents, denies an injunction under the ’920 patent and grants no further stay.
edits.timing: The March and October launch dates allow ten and three months of competition, respectively, in calendar 2027.
edits.event_description: AET applied for approval to sell generic pitolisant with marketing partner Sandoz. The District of Delaware heard the case on Harmony’s ’197 and ’947 patents in February 2026. A separate motion seeks a preliminary injunction under the ’920 patent.
edits.event_timing: The injunction hearing was scheduled for January 26, 2027. The 30-month stay expires February 14. Court decisions were expected around the expiry, but their dates remained open.

baseline.description: With no generic entry in 2027, Harmony earns $268.9 million in WAKIX sales per quarter, its Q3 2026 rate.

scenarios.description: After adverse patent rulings and FDA approval, a generic version of WAKIX launches March 1, 2027. Harmony retains 35% of baseline WAKIX sales over the next ten months.

scenarios.label: Generic launch in October
scenarios.description: Appeal proceedings or interim relief delay a generic WAKIX launch until October 1, 2027. Harmony retains 35% of baseline sales over the final three months.

edits.event: Federal THC limits for hemp-derived products
edits.dependency: RYTHM uses distributors, retailers and its website to sell hemp-derived THC products. Its filing says revenue from the current lineup could fall significantly or cease under the new limit. Distributors can also require RYTHM to repurchase inventory after a regulatory recall or ban.
edits.why_now: Product shipped before the December deadline could be subject to distributor returns. Year-end sales and refund reserves depend in part on how much affected inventory distributors hold.
edits.of: RYTHM’s total 2027 revenue at its Q3 2026 run rate
edits.opening: Brad, RYTHM’s Q3 filing says distributors can require inventory repurchases if the December hemp restrictions take effect. How much product would be eligible for return, and how much of the current lineup could you continue selling in 2027?
edits.why_matters: RYTHM reported $6.36 million in Q3 2026 non-licensing revenue, about 27% of total revenue. A full year without those sales would put 2027 revenue $25.4 million below the Q3 run rate. At Q3’s product gross margin of about 13%, the corresponding gross-profit shortfall would be about $3.4 million.
edits.condition: RYTHM’s current hemp-derived THC products exceed the new per-container limit. The full-year shortfall assumes RYTHM cannot replace those sales with compliant products during 2027.
edits.timing: A December 11 effective date could interrupt sales in the final three weeks of 2026. The two 2027 estimates exclude distributor returns because the filing does not quantify eligible inventory.
edits.event_description: Section 781 of Public Law 119-37 counts THCA toward the 0.3% total-THC limit for hemp and caps total THC in finished cannabinoid products at 0.4 mg per container. Products above the applicable limit lose federal hemp status.
edits.event_timing: The limits affecting RYTHM’s products were scheduled for December 11, 2026, the same day federal funding was due to expire. Congress could change that date or amend the limits in the funding bill or separate legislation.

baseline.description: RYTHM can continue selling its existing products and earns $6.36 million per quarter, its Q3 2026 non-licensing revenue.

scenarios.label: Sales cease throughout 2027
scenarios.description: The federal THC limits take effect in December 2026 and RYTHM makes no sales of its current hemp-derived THC products in 2027.

scenarios.description: Congress permits compliant products in mid-2027. Sales restart in July at half the Q3 2026 rate, yielding one-quarter of baseline annual sales.

edits.event: Possible Supreme Court ruling on state regulation of sports event contracts
edits.dependency: Robinhood earns fees on sports and non-sports contracts. Its CFO said non-sports contracts accounted for about 30% of Q3 event-contract trading. The calculation assigns 70% of aggregate fees to sports based on the remaining trading volume and assumes similar fee rates across categories. The cited records do not break down fees by contract category or state.
edits.why_now: By November 2026, Robinhood had agreed to restrict sports contracts in Nevada, Ohio and Michigan. Kalshi’s December filing was the next scheduled step in New Jersey’s petition.
edits.of: Robinhood’s total net revenue for July–December 2027 at its Q3 2026 run rate
edits.opening: Shiv, you put non-sports contracts at about 30% of event-contract trading in Q3. How closely does that trading mix track the fee mix? If additional states restrict sports contracts, which markets would have the greatest effect on fee revenue?
edits.why_matters: Event contracts accounted for $173 million of Robinhood’s $1.42 billion in Q3 2026 net revenue. If state enforcement removes 90% of estimated sports-contract fees, the modeled shortfall for July through December 2027 is $218 million, or 7.7% of company net revenue at the Q3 rate.
edits.condition: A Supreme Court ruling permitting state enforcement would leave each state to decide how to regulate the contracts. Further state restrictions could also reduce sports trading while the appeals courts remain divided.
edits.timing: Both scenarios cover July through December 2027. Washington’s non-enforcement agreement depends on the Nevada appeals, so restrictions there could start earlier.
edits.event_description: Federal appeals courts split on whether federal commodities law preempts state gaming laws for sports event contracts. The Third Circuit sided with Kalshi in New Jersey. The Sixth and Ninth Circuits sided with states in other cases. New Jersey petitioned the Supreme Court in Flaherty v. KalshiEX, No. 26-299. The petition was pending on November 19, 2026.
edits.event_timing: Kalshi’s response was due December 7, 2026. An early 2027 grant of review could allow a hearing that term. June 30 is the assumed date for a ruling in the larger-shortfall scenario.

baseline.description: Robinhood continues offering sports contracts in the same markets. Total event-contract fees remain at $173 million per quarter for the second half of 2027.

scenarios.label: States can enforce sports restrictions
scenarios.description: The Supreme Court permits state enforcement by June 2027. From July, state restrictions remove 90% of Robinhood’s estimated sports-contract fees. Non-sports fees continue at the Q3 2026 rate.

scenarios.label: Further restrictions in individual states
scenarios.description: The Supreme Court declines review or defers a decision. Additional state restrictions remove 30% of estimated sports fees in the second half of 2027.
